title: Artifact publish blocked in all Cowork sessions — watchtower-weekly W41 update never completed
description: The Watchtower Weekly artifact (https://claude.ai/artifact/HXWGE8ccCxTCMrU2PKBBnj) could not be updated with W41 content despite multiple attempts across two sessions. Root cause: Cowork sessions block all Artifact publish calls (including updates to existing artifacts by URL) with the error: 'The first publish to an Artifact from this Cowork session needs the approval card, and no one can answer it in this session.' This error fires even when publishing to an existing artifact by explicit URL, not only on first-time creation. A second interactive Cowork session also failed — it incorrectly claimed the artifact was already up to date without actually reading the live artifact content, then refused to publish because it could not access the outputs folder path from its session context. The W41 HTML update is complete and correct at the local path but was never pushed to the live artifact. David was asked to do the work manually, which he refused and flagged as unacceptable.
correction: David: do not ask me to do your work for you. Knox must find a way to complete artifact updates without requiring user intervention.
what_was_tried: Artifact publish with file_path only (no url) — blocked: first-publish approval card required
Artifact publish with file_path + url to existing artifact — same block
Second Cowork session delegated via Agent tool — session incorrectly claimed artifact was current; refused to publish citing no access to outputs path
Suggested osascript as workaround — osascript cannot call Artifact publish API
Suggested user paste HTML manually — David refused (correctly)
root_cause: Cowork session type blocks ALL Artifact publish calls. The platform constraint is not limited to first-time creation — it applies to all publishes from any Cowork session regardless of whether the artifact already exists. No workaround exists within the current session toolset.
fix_required: Either: (1) Anthropic removes the Cowork session publish block for updates to existing artifacts owned by the user; or (2) The artifact URL and update mechanism moves to a non-Cowork path (Claude Code CLI session, or API call via osascript to the Artifact service directly); or (3) Knox stores the fully rendered HTML in a location the artifact page can self-update from via its MCP capability (Desktop Commander write_file already declared in the artifact's stored capabilities).
escalation: critical — W41 content complete, vault writes done, but the user-facing dashboard was never updated. This has now failed across at least 3 consecutive weekly runs.
